entry.label: Negative feedback
entry.description: A returned effect that counteracts deviation or change. It often supports regulation and stability, but excessive gain or delay can also create oscillation or instability.
entry.canonical_definition: A feedback relation in which the returned effect opposes a change or deviation in the relevant variable; the reference condition, loop gain, delay and mechanism must be specified.

profile.title: Negative feedback
profile.canonical_definition: A feedback relation in which the returned effect opposes a change or deviation in the relevant variable; the reference condition, loop gain, delay and mechanism must be specified.
profile.summary: Negative feedback returns an effect that opposes deviation or change. It is the basis of many stabilising mechanisms, but its result depends on gain, delay, measurement and the dynamics of the system being regulated.
profile.why_it_matters: The phrase is often used as if negative means criticism or undesirable effects. In technical use it describes loop sign. Poorly timed or overpowered negative feedback can oscillate or destabilise rather than calmly restore a set point.
key_distinctions: explicit set point vs implicit viable range
error correction vs suppression of useful variation
historical_lineage: Rosenblueth, Wiener and Bigelow 1943: goal-directed behaviour and negative feedback
logical_antecedents: deviation or change to be opposed
practice_connections: check whether the correction arrives too late
ask what useful variation is being damped
avoid assuming tighter control is better control
identify who sets the reference condition
common_misreadings: it requires a humanly stated target
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.

claims.statement: Black's 1934 paper provides a primary engineering formulation of stabilised negative-feedback amplification; it does not by itself settle invention priority.
Within the 1943 Rosenblueth–Wiener–Bigelow scheme, negative feedback is an explanatory prerequisite for an important class of purposeful behaviour.
claims.notes: Evidence records: ev_rwb_feedback_purpose. Research pass requires named editorial review before public canonical status.

sources.title: Stabilized Feedback Amplifiers
sources.notes: H. S. Black, Bell System Technical Journal 13(1), pp. 1–18. Primary engineering account of the negative-feedback amplifier principle. The invention predates the paper; this release does not make a first-invention claim.

sources.title: Behavior, Purpose and Teleology
sources.notes: Arturo Rosenblueth, Norbert Wiener and Julian Bigelow, Philosophy of Science 10(1), pp. 18–24. Primary pre-cybernetics article connecting purposive behaviour with input/output relations and negative feedback.
